claims.text: As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a single-phase BCC structure.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a density of approximately 10.21 g/cm³.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a room-temperature yield strength near 1600 MPa.
As-cast HfMoTaTiZr has a yield strength near 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
Replacing approximately 20 at% of Ta with V will reduce the alloy density by roughly 10%.
The Ta-to-V substitution will preserve a room-temperature yield strength near 1600 MPa.
The Ta-to-V substitution will preserve a yield strength near 855 MPa at 1000 °C.
The Ta-to-V substitution will preserve ductility comparable to that of as-cast HfMoTaTiZr.
An optimized Ta-to-V substitution can retain a stable, uniform BCC solid solution.
Ta-to-V substitution reduces the alloy's average atomic weight.
Vanadium's lower atomic weight than tantalum decreases the alloy density.
Vanadium has a valence electron concentration and refractory character similar to tantalum.
The electronic and refractory similarities between V and Ta allow the modified alloy to retain strengthening lattice distortion.
Retained lattice distortion will impede dislocations and sustain solid-solution strengthening.
Optimizing the substitution level can mitigate phase instability and adverse changes in dislocation behavior.
The modified alloys should be evaluated under quasi-static loading at room temperature and 1000 °C using strain rates matching the baseline characterization.

contradictions.description: The phrase '20 at% of Ta' suggests replacement of about 20 atomic-percentage points, which would remove all Ta from an equiatomic HfMoTaTiZr alloy, whereas the proposed 10%, 20%, and 30% replacement series suggests replacing those fractions of the existing Ta content. These interpretations imply substantially different modified compositions.
